text:
maria_net: seeing repeated gRPC streaming stalls between pods in us-west-2 this morning. long-lived streams just stop emitting tokens, client sees no data but TCP stays ESTABLISHED.

alex_sre: +1, alerted by traces. spans show last successful send then nothing for 30s, then client-side retry/reconnect. Any recent infra changes?

maria_net: kernel bump on the node pool last night (5.15.x -> 6.1.x) and we rolled a new cilium version. only affects a subset of nodes (n[12-15]).

dan_runtime: symptoms look like packet fragmentation drops or GSO/TSO mismatch. gRPC streaming is very sensitive to MTU + offload issues. can you capture tcpdump on host and pod?

maria_net: running tcpdump -s 0 -w /tmp/stream.pcap 'host 10.2.14.13 and port 8080' now. also seeing iptables DROP counters bump on node egress.

alex_sre: can you paste output of: ip link show dev eth0; ethtool -k eth0; sysctl net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh?

maria_net: posted outputs:

maria_net: ```
2: eth0: mtu 1500 qdisc mq state UP mode DEFAULT group default qlen 1000
    link/ether 0a:58:...

Features for eth0: rx-checksumming:on tx-checksumming:on scatter-gather:on tcp-segmentation-offload:on tso-v3:on gso:on gro:on

net.ipv4.ipfrag_high_thresh = 262144
```

jess_infra: MTU shows 1500 but our vxlan overlay MTU should be 1450 after encapsulation. if host mtu is 1500 but VXLAN tunnel MTU reduced, fragmentation will occur. kernel change could have altered GSO handling across vxlan.

dan_runtime: also check cilium config: cilium status and whether accelerate-xdp or hardware offloads are enabled. those can introduce sticky fragments if offloads are inconsistent between nodes.

maria_net: cilium-config: vxlan mtu 1450, enable-remote-node-repair=false, offload: enabled. cilium daemonset shows err on n14 about 'encap gso not supported' during startup.

infra-bot: [alert] network.packet_loss.us-west-2: spike on node n14 at 2025-03-03T10:12:09Z -> 2.8% (baseline 0.1%)

alex_sre: ok that 'encap gso not supported' line is suspicious. when GSO/TCP segmentation is not supported through the tunnel, the kernel may try to fragment bigger segments and intermediate devices drop fragments. gRPC streams with large frames (e.g., batched KV cache writes) trigger this.

dan_runtime: quick mitigation: disable GSO/TSO/GRO on the tunnel device or set host MTU to account for vxlan overhead (1500 -> 1450). but disabling offloads might hurt throughput. let's test a fix on a single node.

maria_net: testing by setting `ip link set dev vxlan0 mtu 1450` on n14 and toggling `ethtool -K eth0 gso off tso off gro off` on host. will redeploy a stream test job.

maria_net: after change: streaming resumes, no stalls for 10m during stress test. packet drop counters stopped increasing.

jess_infra: good. plan: patch daemonset hook to set vxlan MTU to 1450 on boot and add a node-check that warns if host netdev supports gso through vxlan. file a runbook for rollback.

alex_sre: long-term we should align kernel versions or upgrade to cilium that handles encap GSO properly. open a ticket linking kernel-change PR and Cilium release notes.

dan_runtime: capture to correlate: tcpdump on pod shows IP fragments previously; after mtu adjustment, no fragments and gRPC frames flow as expected. attach pcaps to ticket.

maria_net: ticket RED-4512 created with logs, pcaps, and temporary mitigation steps. I'll schedule node pool rolling with the MTU fix tonight to avoid recurrence.

alex_sre: thumbs up. add alert that fires when ipfrag_reasm_fail or ip_frag_drop increases above 50/min. also add a dashboard panel for encap gso errors from cilium logs.

jess_infra: and note cost/perf tradeoff: disabling offloads reduces CPU efficiency; track p99 latency and token cost after rollout.

maria_net: thanks team. will follow up after the roll tonight. :thumbsup:
